articles.title: Pope Leo XIV thanks wellwishers in first event after cancer surgery
articles.summary: The Pope's first event since his lung cancer diagnosis and surgery saw him recite the traditional Angelus prayer from the balcony of the Apostolic Palace.
articles.body:
Pope Leo XIV held his first public engagement since his lung cancer surgery on Sunday, as he recited the Angelus prayer from the window of Vatican's Apostolic Palace.

The surgery had taken place just a few days before, after Pope Leo had been diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer.

After the prayer, he thanked the people who have prayed for him in recent days and said he appreciated the support. He added he will now gradually return to his commitments as he recovers.

articles.title: Falta de energia em Uberlândia: canais de atendimento da Cemig | G1
articles.standfirst: Solicitação pode ser feita pelo WhatsApp, telefone, aplicativo, site e SMS. Confira o passo a passo.
articles.summary: A falta de energia em Uberlândia pode ser comunicada pelo WhatsApp, telefone 116, aplicativo e SMS; confira o passo a passo para registrar sua ocorrência na Cemig.
articles.body:
Trabalhador da Cemig realiza manutenção em Uberlândia — Foto: Reprodução/TV Integração

Ficou sem energia em Uberlândia ? A Companhia Energética de Minas Gerais (Cemig) disponibiliza atendimento por WhatsApp, telefone, aplicativo, site, SMS e Telegram para que os consumidores registrem a ocorrência. Mas a concessionária recomenda que o morador faça algumas verificações no imóvel antes de abrir o chamado.

Segundo a Cemig, comunicar a interrupção é importante para que a equipe identifique o problema e trabalhe no restabelecimento do fornecimento.

Ainda de acordo com a empresa, a interrupção no fornecimento pode ocorrer por diferentes motivos, entre eles:

desligamentos programados para manutenção da rede elétrica;

tempestades, ventos fortes e descargas atmosféricas;

acidentes, como colisões de veículos contra postes;

defeitos na instalação elétrica do imóvel;

suspensão do fornecimento por falta de pagamento.

Antes de solicitar atendimento, a Cemig orienta que o consumidor verifique se o problema não está nas instalações do imóvel.

A recomendação é conferir se o disjuntor da caixa de medição e os disjuntores internos estão ligados. Caso estejam desarmados, desligue-os e ligue-os novamente. Se houver cheiro de queimado ou ruído forte durante a verificação, a orientação é interromper o teste e procurar um eletricista.

A Cemig disponibiliza diferentes canais para registrar a ocorrência. São eles:

WhatsApp: adicione o número (31) 3506-1160 aos contatos, envie a mensagem "estou sem luz" e siga as orientações.

Telefone: ligue gratuitamente para o número 116, com atendimento 24 horas.

Aplicativo Cemig Atende: disponível para Android e iOS. Após fazer login, selecione a opção "Estou sem luz".

Cemig Atende Web: faça login no portal e escolha a opção "Estou sem luz".

SMS: envie a mensagem "estou sem luz" para o número 29810 .

Telegram: procure o perfil oficial @CemigOficial e informe a falta de energia ao atendimento automatizado.

Durante a solicitação, a empresa pode pedir o CPF ou CNPJ do titular da instalação, o número da instalação e um telefone celular para contato, caso as equipes precisem falar com o consumidor durante o atendimento.

Quem preferir também pode procurar um posto de atendimento da Cemig em Uberlândia .

Horário de atendimento : de segunda a sexta-feira, das 8h às 16h30.

Como pedir o ressarcimento da Cemig por aparelhos elétricos

Em caso de tempestades, em que há oscilações na rede elétrica ou o retorno da energia após um apagão, alguns aparelhos eletrônicos podem ser danificados por picos de tensão. Os consumidores de baixa tensão, como moradores, pequenos comerciantes e produtores rurais, podem solicitar ressarcimento à Cemig .

O pedido pode ser feito pelo Cemig Atende Web , pelo telefone 116 ou presencialmente em uma agência ou posto de atendimento da companhia. Para registrar a solicitação, o consumidor deve informar:

CPF ou CNPJ e documento oficial com foto

Número da instalação da unidade consumidora (disponível na conta de energia)

Descrição do problema apresentado pelo equipamento

Informações do aparelho danificado, como marca, modelo e características gerais

Telefone celular e e-mail para acompanhamento do processo

A solicitação pode ser feita por um representante, mesmo sem procuração específica. Porém, caso o ressarcimento seja aprovado, o pagamento será realizado ao titular da unidade consumidora na data provável da ocorrência do dano.

O consumidor tem até cinco anos após a ocorrência para pedir o reembolso.

articles.title: Aposta de cidade de 11 habitantes do Paraná acerta todos os números da Lotofácil e ganha mais de R$ 445 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: Apostador paranaense dividiu prêmio principal com dois jogos do interior de São Paulo. Próximo sorteio será realizado nesta segunda (19), com prêmio estimado em R$ 2 milhões.
articles.summary: Apostador paranaense dividiu prêmio principal com dois jogos do interior de São Paulo. Próximo sorteio será realizado nesta segunda (19), com prêmio estimado em R$ 2 milhões.
articles.body:
Uma aposta simples feita em Porecatu , cidade de pouco mais de 11,1 mil habitantes do norte do Paraná, acertou os 15 números do concurso 3807 da Lotofácil, sorteado na manhã deste domingo (18), e faturou R$ 445.386,24 .

O jogo sortudo foi feito na lotérica Pontes e apostou nos 15 números sorteados; ou seja, foi uma aposta mínima e custou R$ 3,50.

🍀 Os números sorteados foram: 01 - 03 - 04 - 07 - 10 - 11 - 13 - 16 - 17 - 19 - 20 - 22 - 23 - 24 - 25.

Outras duas apostas simples também acertaram todas as dezenas e receberam o mesmo prêmio. Uma foi feita em Caçapava e a outra em Mirante do Paranapanema , ambas cidades do interior de SP.

3 apostas acertaram os 15 números e levaram R$ 445.386,24 cada;

341 apostas acertaram 14 números e levaram R$ 1.173,70 cada;

10.878 apostas acertaram 13 números e levaram R$ 35 cada;

115.002 apostas acertaram 12 números e levaram R$ 14 cada;

548.026 apostas acertaram 11 números e levaram R$ 7 cada.

O próximo sorteio será realizado na noite desta segunda-feira (19), com prêmio estimado em R$ 2 milhões.

Foto ilustrativa — Foto: Millena Sartori/g1

Para jogar na Lotofácil, o apostador deve escolher entre 15 e 20 números entre os 25 disponíveis. São premiadas as apostas que acertarem 11, 12, 13, 14 ou 15 dezenas.

A aposta simples, com 15 números, custa R$ 3,50.

É possível apostar em qualquer lotérica do país ou pela internet - no internet banking da Caixa Econômica Federal ou pelo site das Loterias , que podem ser acessados por celular, computador ou outros dispositivos eletrônicos.

Os sorteios regulares são realizados às 21h, de segunda a sexta-feira, e às 11h aos domingos, conforme o calendário da Caixa.

articles.title: Itapeva distribui hipoclorito após laudo apontar alterações na água em meio a surto de virose | G1
articles.standfirst: Análises feitas pelo Instituto Adolfo Lutz apontaram alterações na cor, turbidez e cloração da água. Em cerca de 20 dias, município teve 2,6 mil casos de virose.
articles.summary: Análises feitas pelo Instituto Adolfo Lutz apontaram alterações na cor, turbidez e cloração da água. Em cerca de 20 dias, município teve 2,6 mil casos de virose.
articles.body:
A Secretaria Estadual de Saúde de São Paulo (SES-SP) enviou 40 mil frascos de hipoclorito de sódio à população de Itapeva (SP), após análises apontarem alterações na qualidade da água encanada da cidade. A informação foi confirmada pela pasta via nota, no sábado (17).

🔎 O hipoclorito de sódio é um desinfetante químico, amplamente utilizado para desinfecção e saneamento. Ele elimina bactérias, vírus e parasitas, tornando a água segura para beber.

O município registrou, em cerca de 20 dias, 2,6 mil casos de virose na saúde pública . Os resultados apontaram alterações de cloração, cor e turbidez entre 22 de setembro e 7 de outubro, período em que os atendimentos médicos foram registrados.

As coletas haviam sido encaminhadas para análise no Instituto Adolfo Lutz, em Sorocaba (SP). A água da rede pública seria a fonte comum dos casos de gastroenterite que , até este sábado (17), afetaram 2.686 moradores. As investigações estão em andamento.

Como orientação da secretaria, a população deve consumir alimentos bem cozidos, higienizar corretamente as mãos antes de preparar alimentos e usar hipoclorito de sódio a 2,5%, para desinfecção da água.

Santa Casa de Itapeva (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

Apesar das alterações, a Companhia de Saneamento Básico do Estado de São Paulo (Sabesp) afirmou, também via nota, que não identificou anomalias na água encanada em Itapeva.

A apuração da administração municipal começou após 700 pessoas apresentarem sintomas semelhantes em apenas quatro dias. Entre os principais relatos estão vômitos e diarreia.

O aumento da procura também foi percebido em uma farmácia da cidade, que precisou reforçar o estoque de medicamentos usados no tratamento desses sintomas.

Diego Lipe, médico da Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA) de Itapeva, destaca que a hidratação é fundamental para um paciente que possui suspeita de gastroenterite.

"Hidratação é fundamental porque, quanto mais diarreia, mais desidratada a pessoa física. Não apenas o soro, mas é importante, também, uma hidratação oral", diz.

O Centro de Vigilância Epidemiológica do Estado de São Paulo (CVE-SP) informou em nota que aguarda informações complementares da Vigilância Epidemiológica Municipal para definir as medidas necessárias e dar continuidade às investigações.

Saiba quais são os sintomas de gastroenterite — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

A gastroenterite é uma inflamação do estômago e do intestino e pode provocar sintomas como diarreia, vômitos, náuseas, dores abdominais e febre.

Conforme a Secretaria de Saúde de Itapeva, na maioria dos casos, a recuperação pode ocorrer em casa, com alguns cuidados. A principal recomendação é manter a hidratação, consumindo água, soro de reidratação e outros líquidos ao longo do dia para repor a quantidade perdida pelo organismo.

A alimentação também deve ser mantida, dando preferência a alimentos leves e de fácil digestão, como sopas, frutas e torradas. O repouso é indicado enquanto persistirem os sintomas.

Outro cuidado importante é a higiene das mãos, principalmente após ir ao banheiro e antes de preparar ou consumir alimentos. A medida ajuda a reduzir o risco de transmissão da doença para outras pessoas da casa.

A Secretaria de Saúde também orienta que medicamentos sejam utilizados somente com indicação médica.

articles.title: Was ancient India the world’s forgotten superpower?
articles.summary: In Deja Vu’s latest episode, William Dalrymple explores ancient India’s global influence – and how it was overlooked.
articles.body:
Long before Europe ruled the seas, India’s vast ocean trade linked it to the world. Thinkers like Brahmagupta and Aryabhata spread mathematical ideas that shaped the Renaissance and the modern age. Then colonialism shifted the balance of power. As global power shifts back towards Asia, Deja Vu asks whether the colonial era was the exception.

articles.title: Karmelo Anthony's first fundraiser raised nearly $634,000; family now seeks another $250,000 for murder appeal as questions remain over earlier funds
articles.summary: Karmelo Anthony’s family has launched a new fundraiser seeking $250,000 to pay for his appeal after an earlier campaign raised nearly $634,000.
articles.body: Karmelo Anthony’s family has launched a new fundraiser seeking $250,000 to pay for his appeal after an earlier campaign raised nearly $634,000. The fresh fundraising effort has renewed questions about how the previous donations were spent, particularly after Anthony said he could not afford a lawyer to challenge his murder conviction. According to Fox News, the new campaign is structured differently, with donations intended to go directly into an attorney’s trust account. However, the family’s latest appeal has also drawn criticism online.Why is Karmelo Anthony's family seeking another $250,000The new fundraising campaign was announced at a news conference in Dallas, Texas, following a judge’s rejection of Anthony’s request for a new trial. The 19-year-old was sentenced to 35 years in prison in June 2026 after a jury convicted him of murdering 17-year-old Austin Metcalf during a high school track meet in Frisco, Texas, in April 2025.According to Fox News, the family and its supporters, including attorney Russell Wilson, outlined plans to challenge the conviction through the appeals process. The new campaign aims to raise $250,000 to cover the costs associated with that legal challenge.The money will reportedly be used for legal expenses, including court filings, transcripts, investigators and expert witnesses. Unlike the earlier campaign, the new arrangement places the donations in a trust account administered by Wilson, rather than allowing the family to receive or control the funds directly.The earlier fundraiser covered much more than legal feesThe first campaign, titled ‘Help Karmelo Official Fund,’ was launched on GiveSendGo on 15 April 2025, less than 2 weeks after the fatal stabbing. Organised by Anthony’s mother, Kala Hayes, it initially set a target of nearly $1.4 million and eventually collected just under $634,000.As reported by Fox News, the campaign was not intended to cover legal expenses alone. Its stated purpose also included helping the family relocate because of safety concerns, as well as paying for basic living expenses, transport, counselling and security measures.The family faced threats and unwanted attention as the case attracted national interest. The broader purpose of the fundraiser was presented as a way to help them manage the consequences of the case alongside the legal proceedings.GiveSendGo later confirmed that the donations had been distributed over the preceding year for lawful purposes, including legal defence and family relocation. The platform said the campaign had been closed because its stated purpose had been completed.But the fundraiser's removal following Anthony's conviction did not end questions about the money. Instead, the family's subsequent claim that it needed further financial assistance for his appeal brought the earlier donations back into public discussion.Anthony's claim of financial hardship faces scrutinyThe question of legal expenses became more prominent after Anthony filed a notice of appeal following his conviction. Anthony's court filing described him as unable to afford a lawyer to represent him during the appeal and sought recognition of his financial hardship.The timing attracted attention because hundreds of thousands of dollars had already been raised in his name. Critics questioned why another fundraiser was necessary when the original campaign had collected such a substantial sum.The family’s spokesperson, civil rights activist Dominique Alexander, was questioned about the earlier donations during the news conference announcing the new campaign. Fox News reported that Alexander rejected allegations that the family had used the money improperly but did not provide a detailed breakdown of the previous fund's expenditure.He also declined to explain the family's fees or confirm whether any money from the earlier campaign remained available.The distinction between the two campaigns is important. The original fundraiser explicitly allowed donations to support several family needs, whereas the new campaign says the money will be restricted to legal expenses associated with the appeal.Online criticism grows over the fresh fundraising requestThe new campaign has also prompted a wave of negative reactions on social media. The criticism reflects a broader dispute over how crowdfunding campaigns should communicate their purpose, particularly when donations are collected for someone facing a serious criminal conviction.However, online reactions do not establish that the family misused donations. The earlier campaign's stated terms allowed spending on relocation and living costs as well as legal defence. GiveSendGo has also said the money was distributed for lawful purposes consistent with the campaign's stated objectives.The appeal moves forward as questions remainThe latest fundraising effort marks another stage in Anthony's legal battle, with the new money intended to support his challenge to the murder conviction. His legal team has indicated that the appeal will involve further court filings and may require investigators and expert witnesses.According to Fox News, Anthony maintains that he cannot afford to hire a lawyer for the appeal, despite the substantial sum previously raised on his behalf. His family's supporters argue that challenging the conviction requires further legal work, while critics want clearer answers about the earlier donations.You use AI every day. articles.title: A 12-year-old boy was beside his mother when she passed out while driving at 60 mph, grabbed the wheel and stopped the car before calling 999; now 13, Zac Howells has won a Pride of Britain courage award
articles.summary: For most children, a car journey with a parent is an ordinary part of the day.
articles.body: For most children, a car journey with a parent is an ordinary part of the day. For Zac Howells, one December drive suddenly became a test of instinct, courage and extraordinary composure. At just 12, he found himself trying to control a moving car after his mother lost consciousness behind the wheel. What happened next helped avert what could have been a devastating crash. According to an online report by AOL, now 13, Zac is being recognised with the Child of Courage Award at the Pride of Britain Awards for his actions that day, which not only protected him and his mother but potentially prevented other road users from being caught in a serious accident.A routine journey takes a frightening turnAccording to an AOL report, last December, Zac was travelling with his mother, Nicola Crump, from their home in Ebbw Vale towards a Christmas market in Warwickshire. The journey had begun like any other, with the pair listening to music as Nicola drove along the A40 in Herefordshire. They were travelling at around 60mph when Nicola began to feel unwell. She managed to slow the car and guide it partly onto a narrow verge. Within moments, however, she lost consciousness.The situation became even more dangerous because the automatic car remained in drive. With Nicola's foot still on the accelerator, the vehicle began moving back towards the dual carriageway and gathering speed. Zac immediately realised that something was seriously wrong.A split-second decisionAs per the report, the 12-year-old had no time to wait for help. He reached across from the passenger seat and grabbed the steering wheel, attempting to keep the vehicle under control as it moved towards the central reservation. He steered the car towards the barrier, using it to slow the vehicle until it finally came to a halt. He then switched off the engine and called 999. In the middle of the chaos, Zac also used the car's satnav to establish their location, giving emergency services the information they needed to reach them quickly, adds another report by The Forester.The decision to use the central reservation as a means of stopping the vehicle came with its own risks, but it prevented the car from continuing into the road or potentially leaving the carriageway, adds the online report.Staying focused after the crashThe danger did not end when the car stopped. Nicola remained unconscious for around seven minutes, leaving Zac to deal with the aftermath while waiting for police and paramedics, claims the report by AOL.Emergency responders later found that Nicola had suffered extremely low blood pressure. She is undergoing further cardiology investigations and has not yet returned to driving, informs the AOL report.For Zac, the experience was understandably terrifying. Yet those who responded to the emergency were struck by how composed he remained. His 999 call captured the seriousness of the situation, but also his immediate concern for his mother. That combination of clear thinking and compassion became a defining part of the story.A hero in the eyes of his familyWhen Nicola regained consciousness, she saw emergency lights approaching and was initially confused about what had happened. Zac was physically trembling but remained focused on reassuring her. For his mother, the incident has brought home just how extraordinary his actions were. A journey that began as a simple trip to a Christmas market could easily have ended very differently. Zac's bravery will now be formally recognised at the Pride of Britain Awards, where he will receive the Child of Courage Award at a ceremony at Grosvenor House in London on October 19.Image Courtesy: The ForesterYou use AI every day. articles.title: A working mom started a party-rental side hustle with just $500 and four yard games; within months, Vanessa Romano grew it to 65 bookings and more than $9,000 in revenue without quitting her full-time job
articles.summary: Starting a business does not always require a large investment or a decision to leave a stable job.
articles.body: Starting a business does not always require a large investment or a decision to leave a stable job. For Vanessa Romano, a 39-year-old mother of two, a modest $500 investment in four outdoor party games became the foundation of a growing event-rental business. According to PEOPLE, which profiled Romano on October 12, 2026, her venture, Little Party Co., secured 65 bookings and generated more than $9,000 in booked revenue within its first few months. Romano, who works full-time in corporate communications, launched the business after noticing how party-rental ventures were gaining traction on social media. The idea appealed to her because she could start small, test whether customers were interested and retain the games for her family’s own celebrations if the business did not work out. Rather than investing heavily in equipment or renting commercial premises, she began with four yard games. The relatively low initial cost allowed her to experiment with the business while keeping her regular income intact.From a small experiment to a growing businessThe response was encouraging from the outset. Little Party Co. received five bookings in its first month, generating more than $800 in revenue, enough to recover the initial inventory investment. The following month, 17 bookings brought in more than $1,800. As enquiries increased, Romano began reinvesting the earnings into the business instead of treating the money as additional personal income. Her total investment eventually reached approximately $4,500, while booked revenue climbed to more than $9,000.The growth reflects a practical approach to building a small business: begin with a limited range of products, assess demand and expand only when there is evidence that customers want more. Romano has also learned to be selective about new purchases. Rather than continuously adding equipment to make the rental collection look more impressive, she tracks bookings, considers seasonal demand and prioritises items that customers are actively seeking. This approach helps her manage costs while making decisions about which products could generate enough bookings to justify their purchase.Managing a business alongside a full-time jobRunning Little Party Co. has brought a different set of challenges beyond attracting customers. Romano manages bookings, prepares equipment, cleans and transports the games, and coordinates collections and deliveries around her corporate responsibilities and family commitments. According to her account in PEOPLE, around three-quarters of customers collect their rentals themselves, while the remaining quarter opt for delivery. Depending on the week, she handles between two and eight clients.The physical demands can also be unpredictable. Romano has described fracturing a toe after dropping a cornhole board on her foot, yet still having to complete deliveries that day. The experience illustrates a common difficulty for solo entrepreneurs: when the owner is also responsible for operations, taking time off can be complicated. Time, rather than the initial investment, has become one of her biggest constraints. Growing the business requires work outside her regular office hours, often competing with family time and the need to rest.Why she is not leaving her corporate careerDespite the early success, Romano does not see Little Party Co. as a replacement for her full-time job. She has said she enjoys her corporate career and wants to continue building the rental business alongside it. Her husband has also played an important role in making the arrangement possible, taking on additional household responsibilities while she establishes the venture. For Romano, the business offers a way to pursue her entrepreneurial interests while creating greater financial flexibility for her family.Her experience also reflects a broader appeal of rental-based businesses: equipment can be used repeatedly to generate bookings rather than being sold just once. However, revenue alone does not establish profitability, as expenses such as maintenance, transportation, storage, replacement equipment and taxes must also be considered. Romano's story is a reminder that entrepreneurship does not always have to begin with an all-or-nothing decision. Starting with a small inventory, reinvesting earnings and responding to customer demand allowed her to test a business idea without giving up the security of a regular salary. For now, she is choosing to grow both careers rather than abandon one for the other.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'You'll figure it out': Trump defends Russia sanctions waiver as Republicans, Democrats criticise decision
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has defended his decision to exempt Russia from sweeping sanctions under a new law, calling it a “very good decision” amid
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has defended his decision to exempt Russia from sweeping sanctions under a new law, calling it a “very good decision” amid criticism from lawmakers across party lines.Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida on Saturday evening, Trump said the implications of his decision were not yet fully understood.“A lot of you don’t know what my decision is yet, but we’ll figure it out, and you’ll figure it out,” Trump said, news agency PTI reported.“It’s a very good decision, and it’s going to be a decision that’s good for the country, and I think good for the world because we’re really at a world stage,” he added.Trump on Friday signed an executive order exempting Russia from a new sanctions measure passed by Congress last month. The order also granted a waiver from 100% tariffs on the top five purchasers of Russian oil and gas, including China and India.The exemptions will remain in effect until Trump or the secretary of state, in consultation with the treasury secretary and the US trade representative where appropriate, determines that further action is necessary.Lawmakers from both parties criticise TrumpTrump’s decision has drawn criticism from Republicans and Democrats who had supported the legislation, known as the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.Republican Senator Darline Graham of South Carolina questioned the decision, saying she would prefer to maintain pressure on Moscow to end the war and bring down energy prices.“Personally, I would choose to put the pressure on Russia to end the war and get gas prices down, because I don’t trust Putin, and I don’t trust Russia,” she said.Graham had been endorsed by Trump to fill the Senate seat left vacant following the death of her brother, Senator Lindsey Graham, who had championed the sanctions legislation.Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts accused Trump of disregarding Congress and enabling Putin to continue Russia’s war against Ukraine.Warren urged lawmakers to take action to reverse the decision, adding to the bipartisan criticism of the administration’s approach to sanctions against Moscow.You use AI every day. articles.title: An Ohio boy asked his dad for a baseball field in their backyard; two years and about $30,000 later, the family had its own diamond with infield clay, regulation bases, a raised mound and hand-painted foul lines
articles.summary: An Ohio father spent nearly two years and around $30,000 building a baseball field in his backyard after his five-year-old son asked whether they could
articles.body: An Ohio father spent nearly two years and around $30,000 building a baseball field in his backyard after his five-year-old son asked whether they could have one at home.Jason Kidd, who lived in Brookfield, transformed part of his property into a playing field, with regulation bases, a raised pitcher's mound, professional-grade infield clay and foul lines that he painted himself. The project that involved extensive land preparation, eventually attracted complaints from some neighbours, WSLS 10 News reported in 2019.Kidd's son was playing with a T-ball set when he made the request, which his father initially dismissed. But the idea stayed with Kidd, who began considering whether the family had enough space for a baseball field.The father, who owned a small aircraft management business, eventually started measuring his backyard. The property was not immediately suitable for a playing field and needed a lot of preparation.By the time the main construction was completed, Kidd had spent approximately $30,000. Although the amount was considerable, he said it was close to what he had expected, and worth it to spend time with his son and introduce him to baseball.The biggest expenses came before the field was builtPreparing the property turned out to be one of the most demanding parts of the project. Kidd could not begin laying the playing surface until he had cleared the space and changed the existing landscape.The backyard contained numerous trees, while a hill occupied part of the area intended for the field. Both had to be removed before construction could proceed. Kidd later identified tree removal and insulation work as two of the largest expenses.The baseball surface accounted for only a fraction of the total spending. Kidd estimated that the clay cost between $5,000 and $6,000. Rather than using ordinary soil, he selected the type of material used on major league baseball fields."The field itself wasn't the most expensive," Kidd told Yahoo Lifestyle. "It was five or six thousand dollars worth of clay, the same kind of clay they use on actual big league fields," he added.The completed playing area included regulation bases and a raised pitcher's mound. Kidd also took responsibility for painting the straight foul lines himself.However, the $30,000 expenditure did not cover everything he wanted. A fence was still missing, even though he had expected it to be included within the original budget.Neighbours raised concerns about the backyard projectWhile neighbourhood children were excited about using the field, some residents were less enthusiastic. One concern involved the possible effect on surrounding property values. Kidd recalled that a passer-by had made a negative remark to the contractors working at his home.Another neighbour questioned whether rain could carry material from the playing surface into a nearby ditch. Kidd disagreed with that concern, maintaining that the clay covering the field was too heavy to be washed away in the manner suggested.There were also worries about balls travelling beyond the playing area and breaking windows. Kidd said the field would be used for softball rather than hardball games.The complaints were not limited to conversations with neighbours. According to Kidd, a Brookfield Township trustee had received an anonymous complaint about the project.More additions were planned for the baseball fieldDespite completing the main playing area, Kidd had not finished all the improvements he wanted to make. His plans included a warning track, a fence and a scoreboard.Installing the fence had become a logistical problem. Arranging for steel supplies and fencing contractors to be available together was proving difficult. In July 2019, Kidd said he hoped the work could be completed within the next few weeks.Kidd, a divorced father who shared custody of his son, wanted a place where they could play together and where he could teach the boy about baseball.He was also realistic about how long his son's enthusiasm might last. At five, the boy was interested in baseball, but Kidd recognised that children often change their minds about what they want to do.He explained that his son had already expressed interest in becoming a police officer, a doctor and even a superhero. If baseball eventually stopped being important to him, Kidd said he would accept that. "If he never wants to play a professional sport, that's fine," he said.You use AI every day. articles.body: Demi Moore’s Idaho home brings her close to the natural landscape of Sun Valley, where a river, mountains, and open surroundings shape life beyond Los Angeles. She lives in Hailey, one of three connected towns in the Sun Valley area, which she says feels cosy and familiar, with little main streets, mountains, and clean air.A river runs along the base of her property, giving her a place to swim, kayak, raft, and fly-fish during summer. The surrounding landscape also brings wildlife close to home, with Moore saying she might see a herd of elk in her backyard. In a 2023 interview with the Financial Times, Moore shared how the river and its outdoor activities form part of her life in Idaho.What makes the river at the base of Demi Moore’s Idaho property specialOne of the most distinctive features of Moore’s property is the river at its base. The actress described it as a popular place to spend time during the summer, particularly when the weather makes outdoor activities appealing. She says they sometimes swim there when they’re brave enough, calling the spot the “Redneck Riviera”.The river also provides opportunities for kayaking, river-rafting, and fly-fishing. These activities make the water an important part of how Moore and those who join her enjoy the warmer months. Rather than being limited to a view of the landscape, the river offers a place to get into the water and spend time outdoors.How do mountains, rivers and wildlife shape life around Demi Moore’s Idaho homeMoore’s description of life in Idaho highlights how wildlife can appear close to her home. Speaking about the natural surroundings, she said she might see a herd of elk in her backyard. Her words describe a possibility rather than a regular occurrence, but they show how the landscape around her property brings her close to the region’s wildlife.The river, mountains, and open surroundings contribute to the appeal of the area. For Moore, the setting offers a different atmosphere from Los Angeles, where she also spends time. Her description focuses on the space to breathe and the natural environment that surrounds her Idaho home.Why did Demi Moore’s family turn their Idaho holiday spot into a homeMoore said her connection to Sun Valley began through her former husband, Bruce Willis, who wanted a place there. She had not heard much about the area before her first visit, which took place when their eldest daughter, Rumer, was just 12 days old.The family initially intended to use the property as a holiday spot. When Rumer was approaching school age, however, Moore began questioning why they were staying in Los Angeles. She says that these days she splits her time between Los Angeles and Idaho. Moore said the area feels familiar because she grew up in a small town. She also values its main streets, beautiful mountains, clean air, and family-owned businesses.What makes Sun Valley appealing to Demi Moore beyond its natural sceneryMoore lives in Hailey, one of three connected towns in the Sun Valley area, alongside Ketchum and Bellevue. She described the region as rustic but also cosmopolitan, with an art community and gallery walks that connect local galleries several times a year.The area also changes considerably with the seasons. Moore described summer as a blanket of green and winter as a blanket of white. In winter, she says they tend to stay indoors and play games like Mexican Train dominoes. Her former husband, Bruce Willis, and his wife, Emma, live about a mile away, according to Moore. articles.title: A New Jersey mother’s 1996 will split her estate equally among four children; after her daughter became sole caregiver and a family rift, a new will cut out both sons, and an appeals court has now upheld it
articles.summary: A New Jersey mother who once planned to leave her property equally to her four children later decided that her two sons would receive nothing.
articles.body: A New Jersey mother who once planned to leave her property equally to her four children later decided that her two sons would receive nothing. She made the change in 2016, following a breakdown in their relationship, while one of her daughters had been caring for her for years. After the woman died in 2024, the sons challenged her decision in court, claiming their sisters had influenced her. However, on Friday, a New Jersey appeals court upheld the revised will, finding insufficient evidence that the mother had been pressured into changing it.According to details of the case published by Law.com, the woman signed the will in 1996. At the time, she wanted her estate divided equally among her two sons and two daughters. She also chose one son and one daughter to handle her affairs after her death jointly.That same year, her daughter Deborah became her sole caregiver and began living in the family home. Over the following years, Deborah continued looking after her mother, while relations between the woman and her sons eventually deteriorated.The situation changed in 2015 after a family altercation. The mother's relationship with her sons became strained, and in some periods, they reportedly had no contact. A year later, she signed another will that excluded both sons, and Deborah was also named the sole person responsible for handling the estate after her mother's death.A family rift, a new will and a legal challengeThe disagreement over this decision did not reach court immediately. The mother continued living for another eight years, during which questions were raised about whether someone close to her was taking advantage of her financially.In 2021, New Jersey's Adult Protective Services Programme investigated a complaint alleging financial exploitation. The investigation did not find evidence to substantiate the allegation, and the matter was closed.When the mother died in 2024, one of her sons objected to the revised will. Both sons subsequently challenged the arrangements, questioning whether their mother had made the decision independently.Their argument focused largely on the relationships she shared with her daughters. Deborah had been her caregiver since 1996, and the mother was also close to her other daughter. The sons believed these circumstances raised doubts about whether she had acted entirely of her own choice.Sons believe their mother was influencedThe sons argued that their mother's dependence on Deborah for care, together with her close relationship with their other sister, should have prompted greater scrutiny of the 2016 will. They wanted the court to require their sisters to demonstrate that their mother had not been improperly influencedThe daughters rejected these claims. They maintained that there was no evidence their mother had been controlled or persuaded to change her will against her wishes.The court examined the family's history, including the mother's deteriorating relationship with her sons and the circumstances in which she had prepared the revised document.One important detail was that neither daughter had initiated the preparation of the 2016 will. Neither was present when their mother signed it.The court also considered whether the mother had been capable of making her own decisions at the time. No medical evidence from that period showed that her ability to understand or manage her affairs had been impaired.Why did the court uphold the mother's decision?The judge who first heard the case found that the mother's relationship with her sons had already been damaged for years before her death. The 2016 will was also consistent with decisions she made later about her estate.The court did not accept that Deborah's role as caregiver automatically meant she had control over her mother's financial decisions.The sons appealed, but the New Jersey Superior Court's Appellate Division reached the same conclusion.In its October 16 ruling, the appeals court found that the brothers had failed to provide sufficient evidence that either sister had improperly influenced their mother. It also agreed that there was no basis to require the daughters to prove the absence of such influence.The judges considered the mother's ability to manage her own affairs, the absence of evidence of pressure when the revised will was signed and the history of her relationships with her children.You use AI every day. articles.title: Can hackers get into your fridge? Your smart home may be less safe than you think
articles.summary: A fridge keeping tabs on your groceries is useful. A hacker keeping tabs on your fridge is a different story.
articles.body: A fridge keeping tabs on your groceries is useful. A hacker keeping tabs on your fridge is a different story.The growing use of internet-connected equipment has created new cybersecurity risks, even for devices once considered purely mechanical. Recently, hackers sabotaged refrigeration systems at hundreds of French supermarkets, exploiting equipment that can now be monitored and controlled remotely.From heating systems and security cameras to alarm networks and household appliances, more devices are connecting to the internet, creating potential entry points for cybercriminals.Is your fridge hackable?In theory, yes. Any refrigerator connected to the internet, directly or through an app, cloud service or home network, could potentially be hacked.In 2015, researchers demonstrated at a hacking conference in Las Vegas how a Samsung smart refrigerator could be compromised, allowing them to intercept some of the internet traffic passing through it.However, hackers may not necessarily want to control an appliance. Their objective could be to steal information, disrupt services or use the device to gain access to a larger network.From smart locks to toothbrushes: What is vulnerable?Potential targets include security cameras, video doorbells, alarm systems, smart locks, thermostats and central heating systems. Refrigerators, ovens and washing machines can also be vulnerable when connected to the wider internet. Even some toothbrushes now have internet connectivity.However, routers account for more than three-quarters of attacks on connected devices, according to security-industry data.As manufacturers add internet connectivity to products that once operated independently, the number of potential entry points for attackers continues to grow.What can hackers do?Once inside a device, hackers can gather information or take control of its functions. A compromised camera could reveal the inside of a home, while a device with a microphone could pick up sound. A hacked router could expose information travelling across the network.Attackers may also switch devices on or off, change settings or lock users out of their accounts. A compromised thermostat could affect heating, while a hacked refrigerator or freezer could have its temperature controls disrupted.Poorly secured devices may also allow hackers to access other systems on the same network or steal personal information linked to online accounts.How far can hackers go?Connected vehicles have also been found to have cybersecurity vulnerabilities. In 2015, researchers remotely took control of a moving Jeep through its internet-connected entertainment system. The incident led to a recall of about 1.4 million vehicles and the deployment of software fixes, Reuters reported.Nearly a decade later, researchers disclosed a flaw that allowed them to track, unlock and start certain Kia vehicles using only a licence plate number. They reported the vulnerabilities to Kia, which fixed them within months. There was no evidence that the flaws had been exploited in real-world attacks.Modern vehicles and aircraft have extensive safety and backup systems. Electricity and water networks also have multiple layers of security, monitoring and regulation that are generally absent from consumer devices.While critical infrastructure is not immune to cyber attacks, it is typically harder to target than a household appliance connected to Wi-Fi.How can you protect your devices?Cybersecurity experts recommend changing default passwords, enabling two-factor authentication wherever available and regularly installing software updates.Devices that no longer receive security updates should be removed or replaced. Consumers should also keep most devices on a local network and connect products to the wider internet only when there is a clear reason to do so.The simplest precaution is to limit the number of connected devices. The fewer potential entry points there are, the fewer opportunities attackers have to exploit them.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Driver, owner arrested after speeding truck rams devotees near Gwalior temple; 15 killed
articles.summary: BHOPAL: A heavy truck ploughed into devotees at the Sheetla Mata Temple fair on Chinor Road in Gwalior around 1.30am on Sunday, killing at least 15 people
articles.body: BHOPAL: A heavy truck ploughed into devotees at the Sheetla Mata Temple fair on Chinor Road in Gwalior around 1.30am on Sunday, killing at least 15 people and injuring 26 others, including two police personnel. Two Home Guard jawans posted at the entry point were among those killed. The death toll could rise, as several injured people remain in critical condition.The central question is how heavy trucks reached the shrine despite restrictions on all vehicles, including bicycles, on the route during the nine-day festival. Victims’ families and local residents questioned how the trucks passed barricades placed some distance from the temple. Authorities have yet to explain how the vehicles entered the restricted stretch.The accident occurred on Saptami of Sharadiya Navratri, when the shrine was crowded with devotees. Chief Minister Mohan Yadav removed the Jhansi Road city superintendent of police (CSP) and suspended eight other police personnel. The truck’s owner and driver were arrested in Dholpur.Collector Ruchika Chauhan confirmed the incident. Hospital authorities initially reported 13 deaths and said seven of the injured were in critical condition. The death toll later rose to 15. Officials said they were collecting details of patients admitted to other hospitals.How the truck reached the crowd remains disputedSome accounts suggest that two trucks were parked on the steep road and that one rolled downhill after its brakes failed. Others say one of the trucks broke through the barricades and entered the restricted stretch.Officials said the drivers of two overloaded trucks, unfamiliar with the route and relying on GPS-based navigation, were directed towards the temple road. According to reports, the trucks, which were heading to Punjab, approached the rear of the temple from the direction of Chinor at night.On reaching a downward slope, the drivers saw a crowd of around one lakh people below. The brakes of one truck reportedly failed, causing it to roll downhill and crush devotees walking along the roadside before crashing into the temple’s entrance gate.Part of the wall collapsed, trapping several people under the debris. An eyewitness said he and his companions were walking towards the temple when the truck appeared to lose its brakes and ploughed into the crowd.Local journalist Puneet Srivastava, who was at the spot during the rescue operation, said two trucks were involved. He added that the death toll could have been much higher had the temple’s 200-year-old wall not stopped the truck.Several relatives said the lane was so narrow that even a bicycle could barely pass. A relative of Sarla Tomar, who died while on her way to the temple, questioned who had allowed the trucks to enter from the rear.CSP removed, eight police personnel suspendedChief Minister Yadav removed Jhansi Road CSP Ravi Bhadauria for alleged negligence and suspended eight other police personnel, taking the total number of those facing action to nine.The suspended personnel are Jhansi Road SHO Shakti Singh Yadav, Antri SHO Gitesh Sharma, Jhansi Road Traffic SHO Abhishek Raghuvanshi, Traffic Inspector Raghavendra Jadon, Head Constable Sushil Dwivedi, and Constables Kishan Khanna, Anil Jaitpuria and Pawan Sengar.Yadav said the safety of devotees was paramount and that negligence in the line of duty would not be tolerated. He added that accountability would be fixed.Speaking to reporters at Indore airport, he said a detailed inquiry would be conducted and strict action taken against those found responsible.Truck owner and driver arrestedPolice arrested truck owner Mohit Singh and driver Dilbag Singh in Dholpur. The arrests were made by the Jhansi Road police station team.Police said the two men had jumped out of the truck and fled after the accident. They are being questioned.Anger and protestsResidents and devotees blocked the road, demanding strict action against reckless drivers and a complete ban on heavy vehicles in the area.Additional police personnel were brought in from other stations, and a large contingent remained deployed through the night.Tension also flared outside the post-mortem facility, where relatives had gathered to identify the dead. Some raised slogans against the police administration, prompting the deployment of additional personnel.When Senior Superintendent of Police Dharmveer Singh arrived, relatives demanded answers about how the trucks had entered the restricted area and how the deaths had occurred.Mother alleges delay in treatmentA mother whose teenage son died in the accident alleged that he was still breathing after the crash and that she wanted to take him to a private hospital.She claimed that police insisted he be taken for a post-mortem examination, struck the ambulance with sticks and forced it to leave. She alleged that the delay contributed to her son's death.Compensation and reactionsThe state government will provide Rs 4 lakh to the family of each person killed, Rs 2 lakh to each seriously injured person and Rs 50,000 to each of the other injured, Yadav said in a social media post. All the injured will receive free treatment.The affected families are from Gwalior, Shivpuri and Sheopur. Yadav asked ministers Edal Singh Kansana and Rakesh Shukla to reach Gwalior. He also prayed to Baba Mahakal for peace for the departed souls and a speedy recovery for the injured.President Droupadi Murmu said in a social media post that the loss of lives was distressing and conveyed her condolences to the bereaved families.Union minister Jyotiraditya Scindia described the accident as extremely painful and said his heart was deeply troubled.Rescue and relief operationsLocal residents, devotees and police personnel pulled victims from the wreckage. Many had suffered head injuries and fractures.SSP Dharmveer Singh and Additional Superintendent of Police Shivesh Baghel reached the spot with personnel from several city police stations and senior administrative officials.One young woman, Kalpana Parihar, was trapped beneath a truck's wheel. She had gone to the temple with her relative Gaurav Parihar, who was among those killed. Police freed her by letting the air out of the tyre.She suffered severe injuries to the lower part of her body and is in the intensive care unit of the trauma centre.Seriously injured victims were rushed to the trauma centre at Jaya Arogya Hospital in a goods vehicle rather than wait for ambulances. Ambulances continued to transport the dead and injured until around 4am.The injured were taken to the Gwalior Trauma Centre and the 1,000-bed hospital, where the collector and senior police officers reviewed treatment arrangements.A crane was used to lift the overturned truck and reach people trapped beneath it. The first hydra machine to arrive developed a technical fault, prompting a request for a second machine from the agency constructing an elevated road nearby. A report filed during the rescue operation said the second machine had yet to arrive.The deadThe deceased were identified as Satendra Singh Gurjar (22), Sarla Tomar (50), Gaurav Parihar (18), Mahesh Sharma (45), Vimlesh Badhel (18), Devesh Badhel (17), Prince alias Chhotu Jatav (16), Shaurya Sharma (15), Hemant Rathore (age not recorded), Divyansh Kushwah (17), Pawan Rathore (23), Lav Tyagi (15), Aman Tyagi (13), Ashok Tyagi (45) and Nitesh alias Ritesh (18).Aman Tyagi, 13, was the youngest victim. Among those whose ages were recorded, Sarla Tomar, 50, was the oldest.Pawan Rathore, a resident of Gadaipur in Hazira, had gone to the temple to pray when he was killed.Families search for missing relativesFamilies scrambled to find relatives who had accompanied them to the temple.A relative of Divyansh Kushwah said the group had left after offering prayers but could not find him. They searched for him, informed the police and eventually found him after returning inside.The brother-in-law of a shopkeeper near the temple said the injured man could not recall how the accident had happened and remembered only smoke and confusion.Another injured devotee, who suffered fractures in both legs, was put on a ventilator, a relative said. His family learnt about the accident around 5am and found him in critical condition at the hospital.Fair draws large crowds on SaptamiThe ancient Sheetla Mata Temple in Sataun village on Chinor Road attracts large crowds during the nine-day Sharadiya Navratri festival, particularly on Saptami.Villagers believe that visiting the shrine on this day brings blessings for children and relief from illness. articles.title: France's 140 year old Town Hall survived World Wars but succumbed to protesters' fury
articles.summary: A 143-year-old town hall in the French city of Limoges, which served as a hub for resistance activities during Nazi occupation and hosted Belgium’s
articles.body: A 143-year-old town hall in the French city of Limoges, which served as a hub for resistance activities during Nazi occupation and hosted Belgium’s government-in-exile in 1940, has been largely destroyed after protesters set it ablaze during violent demonstrations over the cost of living, school conditions and public services.Local officials said around two-thirds of the historic building had been destroyed in the fire, describing the damage as a “catastrophe for heritage”.The destruction came as protests swept across France on Saturday, with demonstrations over rising fuel prices, inflation and deteriorating public services turning violent in several cities. An estimated 550,000 people took part in the marches, according to the French interior ministry.Also Read | Student grievances, cost-of-living crisis, political discontent: Why are protests turning violent in FranceDozens of shops were looted in cities including Paris, Marseille, Nice, Nantes, Bordeaux, Limoges, Lille, Toulouse and Strasbourg. Fires burned in Paris late into the evening, while riot police used tear gas and baton charges to disperse crowds.The damage to Limoges town hall has put the spotlight on a building with a significant place in the city's wartime history.In May 1940, as Nazi Germany advanced across Europe, Belgian ministers and parliamentarians who had fled their country arrived in Limoges on May 31. They had briefly taken refuge in Poitiers before moving to Limoges, where they were welcomed by the city's then mayor, Léon Betoulle.Also Read | France protests leave Paris streets buried in rubbish amidst violence, looting across nationThe Belgian representatives condemned King Leopold III's decision to surrender to the Nazi threat and established their offices in the town hall and the prefecture. Belgian flags were flown alongside French ones, turning the municipal building into a centre of activity for the government-in-exile.During the German occupation of France, the town hall also became an important base for the Resistance in the southern unoccupied zone.Lucien Berdasé, who worked in the municipal administration, helped resistance fighters by sabotaging lists of Jewish residents, preparing false documents and concealing weapons stored in the building. He also arranged travel permits for vehicles used by the *Maquis*, the French resistance fighters.Suzanne Rodi-Boyer, who was responsible for distributing food ration cards at the town hall, helped Jewish families obtain false papers using stamps taken from the municipality. These efforts made the building part of a wider network that helped people evade Nazi persecution and supported resistance activities.The town hall's post-war history included a visit by General Charles de Gaulle on March 4, 1945. Georges Guingouin, a prominent Resistance figure and member of the Order of Liberation, later served as Limoges mayor from April 1945 to October 1947.The latest destruction comes amid wider unrest across Europe over economic pressures and public services. In France, the demonstrations followed student-led protests last month and expanded into a broader movement against rising living costs and what protesters described as government inaction.French President Emmanuel Macron condemned those responsible for violence and looting, warning that people who attacked public offices, businesses and town halls would face prosecution and punishment.At least 195 people had been detained amid criticism of the authorities' handling of the demonstrations.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Not food poisoning; it is murder': Twist in Noida family deaths as dispute over property emerges
articles.summary: NOIDA: A property dispute within the family has emerged as a key allegation in the deaths of a couple and their three minor children, who were found dead
articles.body: NOIDA: A property dispute within the family has emerged as a key allegation in the deaths of a couple and their three minor children, who were found dead at their home in Nagla Shri Padam village on Saturday morning.Relatives have accused the deceased man's mother, Chandravati, of transferring family land and houses to her three daughters, allegedly leaving Mahesh and his family distressed about their future. The allegations have not been established, and the cause of death remains uncertain.“This is not food poisoning; it is murder. My sister's sister-in-law and her husband orchestrated the deaths over a property dispute,” alleged Pooja, Lalita's sister.The deceased were identified as Mahesh (37), his wife Lalita (35), and their children Laddu (11), Mishti (7) and Sakshat (3).There were no visible injuries on any of the victims, but all were found frothing at the mouth. Food poisoning was initially suspected, though a preliminary inspection by food safety officials did not conclusively point to it.Child climbs boundary wall, finds family unresponsiveThe deaths came to light on Saturday morning when a child from the neighbourhood went to call Mahesh's two school-going children for an examination. When nobody responded, the child climbed the boundary wall and found the family unresponsive inside the house.Mahesh and one of the children were found on a cot, while Lalita and the other two children were on a bed. One of the children was found clinging to the mother's lap, according to the account of the scene.Relatives allege mother transferred property to daughtersRelatives alleged that disputes over the family's property had been frequent and that Chandravati had repeatedly asked Mahesh and his family to vacate the house. They accused her and one of her daughters of being involved in the deaths, but the allegations remain unproven.Satendra Jatav alleged that Chandravati had threatened to make Mahesh's family leave and said the property would go to her daughters. Neighbours also claimed that arguments over property were common in the family.Mahesh's brother Rahul died by suicide in 2019. Relatives alleged that he, too, had been distressed over the distribution of family property.Family received Rs 1.25 crore compensation in 2009According to Lalita's brother Sonu, Chandravati had inherited property from her husband and her maternal family in Rabupura. In the early 2000s, Mahesh's father, Kishan Lal, who originally belonged to Khera Kalan village in Delhi's Narela, bought around 10 bighas of land in Nagla Padam, which relatives described as Chandravati's maternal village.In 2009, the family received around Rs 1.25 crore in compensation from the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA), along with a plot under its 7% developed-plot scheme.Relatives alleged that the compensation and plot benefits went to Chandravati's three daughters, leaving her two sons without a share.Sonu said the funds were used to build a house in Rabupura after Mahesh married in 2017. Mahesh lived there with Lalita, while Chandravati moved in about a year before the deaths.Relatives cite property transfers after father's deathRelatives alleged that after Kishan Lal died in 2023, Chandravati transferred the family's ancestral house in Delhi to two of her daughters. They also claimed that she sold a 167-sq-metre house in Nagla Padam on August 18, 2025.According to the relatives, around six months ago, Chandravati transferred about 10 bighas of land to one of her daughters and her husband, along with the house where Mahesh's family lived.The details of the alleged transfers and the relatives' claims about the distribution of property have not been independently established.'He said he would ensure I got my share'Neeraj, Rahul's wife, said she was forced to leave the family home after her husband's death and was not allowed to continue living there with her 14-year-old daughter. The two now live in a rented house, she said.“Mahesh used to say, ‘My brother is gone, but I won't deprive you of your share. I will ensure you get what is rightfully yours.’ My mother-in-law always takes her daughters' side,” Neeraj said, describing Mahesh and Lalita as good people.Relatives say family showed no signs of distressSonu said Mahesh's family had visited his home around 10 days before the deaths and appeared normal. He added that he had spoken to the family over the phone two days earlier, but they had not mentioned any problems or distress.The cause of the five deaths remains unclear. articles.body: Donald Trump has taken a swipe at France over its history of revolutions, joking that Americans receiving his proposed $5,000 payment could head to the European country to “join the revolution” as protests over the cost of living and public services swept French cities.According to the transcript of his October 16 rally in Dalton, Georgia, Trump made the remarks while discussing his proposed $5,000 payment to adult Americans, which he said would be conditional on Republicans winning both chambers of Congress in the November midterm elections. He joked about how a couple might spend the money abroad before reiterating that it would have to be spent in the United States.Trump jokingly said, “Darling, the president just sent us $5,000. Let's go to France. It's a lovely place. No riots. No revolutions. You know, France seems to be so damn good for revolutions. It's unbelievable. Let's go to France and join the revolution and spend our $5,000 there.”Trump had earlier said the proposed payment would come with a condition that recipients spend the money in the United States.“The only caveat is you have to spend that $5,000 in the United States of America,” he said, adding that the money could not be spent in countries such as China, Japan and France.The remarks came as France witnessed nationwide demonstrations, with trade unions, students and other groups taking to the streets over rising living costs, wages, education conditions and concerns about public services.The protests reflected mounting frustration over economic pressures and perceived inequalities, adding to political challenges facing the French government ahead of the 2027 presidential election.You use AI every day. articles.title: ​Florida permanently protects nearly 1,500 acres across two cattle ranches with $8.7 million in conservation easements, preventing future development while preserving farmland and wildlife
articles.summary: Florida has added two more ranches to its growing list of protected agricultural lands, with nearly 1,500 acres in Manatee and Highlands counties secured
articles.body: Florida has added two more ranches to its growing list of protected agricultural lands, with nearly 1,500 acres in Manatee and Highlands counties secured from future development. The ranches are now permanently protected through the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services’ Rural and Family Lands Protection Program, Florida Commissioner of Agriculture Wilton Simpson said in a release. These rural land easements prevent future development while allowing agricultural operations to continue and contribute to Florida’s economy and the production of food, timber and other resources vital to the state’s prosperity.“I’m proud to announce today the preservation of two additional working Florida agricultural operations, which builds on the historic progress we’ve made through the Rural and Family Lands Protection Program,” Commissioner Wilton Simpson said in a statement. “My goal is to secure the permanent future of agriculture in Florida, and the Rural and Family Lands Protection Program gives us the most effective and cost-efficient way to preserve our natural lands from development while also supporting our farmers and ranchers.”Since the program began, Florida has protected more than 253,000 acres of farmland, including nearly 188,000 acres under Commissioner Simpson’s administration. The newly protected properties lie within the Florida Wildlife Corridor and are enrolled in the department’s Best Management Practices (BMP) programme.Mossy IslandMossy Island covers about 420 acres used for cattle farming, and its location does much of the work. It sits next to Myakka River State Park to the west and Myakka Prairie Conservation Easements to the south, so it already borders protected land. The surrounding area consists mostly of pasture, with some cropland and scattered low-density housing. Mossy Island is protected from future development through a $4 million conservation agreement, with $500,000 contributed by Manatee County.The state’s announcement also points to the threat. Land along the property’s northern boundary is projected to be developed by 2040, according to University of Florida projections. The easement is intended to prevent that development.Florida Commission Company RanchFlorida Commission Company Ranch sits in Highlands County and covers about 1,046 acres. The farmland is now permanently protected from development through a rural land protection easement totalling $4.7 million. The ranch raises cattle on pastures and natural areas and grows hay for on-site use.What is the Rural and Family Lands Protection Program?In 2001, Florida established the Rural and Family Lands Protection Program Act, which recognises the importance of working agricultural lands to the state’s economic future. This helps preserve farmland as development puts increasing pressure on rural areas. The programme works with farmers and ranchers to keep agricultural land in use and protect natural resources.The state pays landowners to restrict future development under conservation agreements, but not to stop farming and ranching. This allows the land to continue producing food and timber while also helping the state avoid the long-term costs of buying and managing conservation land itself.Since 2022, Commissioner Wilton Simpson has helped secure more than $1.1 billion in state funding for the programme, including $425 million in the 2026–27 state budget. Simpson has also played a key role in Florida’s land conservation policy long before becoming the state’s Commissioner of Agriculture. During his tenure as Senate President, he backed the Florida Wildlife Corridor Act, which aims to connect and protect natural habitats across the state while keeping working agricultural lands safe from future development.Meanwhile, Mossy Island and Florida Commission Company Ranch sit within that corridor. Both are enrolled in the state’s Best Management Practices programme, a set of environmental practices for working land. The easements protect the land from development, while the ranchers continue farming under those practices.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Balochistan unrest: Teacher's killing sparks outrage, kin say Pak officials shielding 'death squads'
articles.summary: The alleged torture and killing of a teacher in Pakistan’s restive Balochistan province triggered protests by his family members and local residents, who
articles.body: The alleged torture and killing of a teacher in Pakistan’s restive Balochistan province triggered protests by his family members and local residents, who warned that a key highway would be blockaded if authorities failed to take action.The protesters accused Pakistani forces of shielding those allegedly responsible for the death of Parvez Mazar, an Arabic teacher at Government High School Babbar Shor in Pasni, a coastal town in Balochistan’s Gwadar district, The Balochistan Post reported.According to Mazar’s relatives, he was "taken away" in front of his family on Tuesday and was found dead the following day. They claimed that members of a state-backed armed group, described as a “death squad,” took him to a private torture facility, where he was detained and killed.Protesters, including Mazar’s children, gathered outside the Pasni Press Club, demanding the immediate arrest of those responsible for his death. They demanded accountability and justice for the deceased teacher's family.The demonstrators warned that failure to address their demands would prompt them to stage a sit-in at Pasni Zero Point and block the Makran Coastal Highway, a key route connecting Gwadar with Karachi in Sindh province, Pakistan’s largest city and the country's financial and commercial hub.They demanded that state institutions take action against armed groups accused of abducting, torturing and killing civilians while allegedly operating under the protection of state agencies.What are Balochistan's 'death squads'?Baloch rights organisations and activists use the term “death squads” to describe armed groups they allege receive support or protection from Pakistani state institutions.These groups have been accused of targeting civilians, political activists and human rights defenders in Balochistan, a province long affected by an insurgency and a security crackdown.(With ANI inputs)You use AI every day. articles.title: A Norfolk woman inherited a homemade 1970s model village and grew it into a front garden attraction with more than 20 miniature buildings
articles.summary: Some hobbies start small and quietly take over.
articles.body: Some hobbies start small and quietly take over. For Jane High, it began with a love of miniature figures and ended with a front garden that draws smiles from passers-by. She was given a homemade 1970s model village, rebuilt it after it arrived in pieces, and has kept adding to it ever since. Today it has more than 20 tiny buildings, from a fish and chip shop to a windmill, plus some truly unexpected visitors. Read on to discover where this little village came from, how she brought it back to life, and why it makes so many passers-by smile.Meet Jane High, the Scratby woman who turned a 1970s model village into a quirky front garden attractionA front garden in Scratby, near Great Yarmouth in Norfolk, has become a quirky local attraction. According to the BBC, the garden belongs to Jane High, who was gifted a homemade model village from the 1970s four years ago. She has not simply preserved it; she has continued to add to it, and it now displays more than 20 tiny buildings. High told the BBC that the village started as a little hobby that has taken over, and that its purpose is to make people smile as they walk past. The report describes the project as giving the models a new lease of life, turning what was once a private garden display into something the whole neighbourhood can enjoy.Where the village began, Alan Sewell's concrete houses, moulds, and church in a north London gardenThe story begins long before Scratby. The village was originally in Alan Sewell's north London garden, where it was said to have been built by Sewell himself. He made moulds, concrete houses, and a church to display there. After Sewell died in 2006, his daughter inherited the village, and it was moved to Great Yarmouth. Concrete construction is a notable detail, because it suggests a project intended to last outdoors, and it helps explain how the village could survive a move. The report's careful wording, saying the village was said to have been built by Sewell, also reminds readers that homemade projects like this often rely on family memory rather than formal records, which makes the care shown by its new keeper all the more valuable.From painting figures in Great Yarmouth to rehoming a village, how Jane High's love of models beganHigh's affection for miniature worlds has its own backstory. She told the BBC that she was not into dolls or doll houses as a child, yet many years ago she tried her hand at painting model figures. She used to paint figures for the model village in Great Yarmouth, and she believes that is where her love of the hobby began, adding that she absolutely loves that village. After Sewell's village moved to Great Yarmouth, she passed it every day and thought it needed a bit of love and attention. When she met Sewell's daughter by chance, the two agreed that High was the right person to rehome it. The sequence shows how a hobby can lead naturally into a larger project, with small skills and shared enthusiasm eventually turning into a garden full of miniature buildings.Rebuilding a dismantled village, a summer of digging the lawn, laying concrete roads, and raising a hillMoving the village was no small task. It had to be dismantled before transport and arrived at High's house in Scratby in pieces, after which she spent a summer putting it all back together. Part of her front lawn had to be dug out so concrete roads could be laid. Nothing was wasted: everything that came out of the ground was piled into a big heap, and that heap became the hill on which the church now stands. The detail is a charming example of landscape thinking on a miniature scale, using the garden itself as raw material rather than hauling soil away. It also shows the effort behind the attraction, which relied on digging, rebuilding, and patience before a single visitor could stop to admire it.A fish and chip shop, a forge, a windmill, and Daleks, the quirky scenes that make visitors smileToday the miniature village plays out numerous scenes, including a 1960s garage, a forge, and a windmill. Fitting for a coastal setting, there is also a fish and chip shop. Not everything fits neatly together, High told the British Broadcasting Corporation that the village includes things that do not really belong, such as dinosaurs, Doctor Who figures, and Daleks, because children keep coming over. She explained that the unconventional mix is a response to her young visitors, who have effectively shaped the display. For High, the point is simple, "It just makes people smile when they come past." For readers looking for a reminder that small acts of creativity can brighten a street, a front garden in Scratby offers one.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
